pageCache.text:
Welcome to our school website! We hope that you can find everything you wish to know about our lovely school. If there is anything that you would like to know more about, please don’t hesitate to contact us.
Welcome!
I am Beccy Harris and I am delighted to be the headteacher of St. Barnabas CE Primary School. We are a small school for children aged 3-11, set in the very centre of the city of Oxford, and surrounded by its most famous landmarks and institutions.
We are a happy, thriving school, rich in self belief and community spirit . Our pupils come from the local communities of Jericho and Summertown as well as from further across the city. We also welcome families from all over the world who are brought to Oxford to work and study. Our diverse international perspective is part of the St. Barnabas vibrancy that we are so well known for.
Children achieve well as St. Barnabas. We are a dynamic and highly successful staff team who have demonstrated our commitment to high academic outcomes, achieved by focusing on a stimulating and engaging curriculum that is delivered through excellent teaching by inspiring teachers.
Local press coverage 2024.
Local press coverage 2025
Our school is a warm empathetic environment where children flourish in all aspects of their development. Children build good relationships, feel valued and are listened to. We cherish them as unique individuals with an innate abundance of enthusiasm and talent. We strive to make school inspiring, enjoyable and a great place to create lifelong childhood memories. Parents are welcomed into the school at every opportunity because we know that is good for everyone!
In March 2025, our Ofsted Inspection awarded us a strong ‘GOOD’ grading in all areas. As well as strong academic outcomes, the school is described as a ‘happy place to be’ with ‘warm relationships’, ‘kindness’ and ‘harmonious social times’. It is also noted that we offer ‘a range of opportunities to nurture talents and interests’ and have ‘a strong emphasis on pupil’s character, individuality and personal development’.
As we press on from ‘GOOD’ to great, we continue to excel in our provision for more able learners, but are also focused on the wider curriculum and the experiences that we offer. Read about this term’s inspiring art exhibition at:
https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cgjpgv45zg2o
Which builds on our previous community art piece
https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx2jlg43jlro
Since the school video was made the grounds have been developed with a new sandpit for older children, a mud kitchen, an outdoor workshop and a designated forest school shelter. A sports cage is being installed this Autumn. Progress is unstoppable!
Our school vision is:
‘They will soar on wings like eagles’’ (Isaiah 40:31)
Through values that create AWE-some individuals, we will become A (Adventurous) W (Wise) and E (Encouraging).
We are a fully inclusive Church of England school welcoming children of all faiths and world views. Through their own lens, children are encouraged to explore moral and spiritual values and are given the space to consider the bigger questions in life. This helps them grow a deeper understanding of themselves and the world around them giving them a strong sense of their identity, purpose and future direction.
So what next? We have secured funding for an enhanced pathway provision enabling us to open a new class in September 2026. This provision will support SEN children who struggle to access class-based learning. This important new initiative will ensure that all our children, no matter what barriers they experience, are given every opportunity to thrive.
Please look at our school video (below) . In the meantime, take the time to explore the website for information about the school. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any questions or would like to find out more. We look forward to welcoming you to our school soon.
Quick Links
“Pupils feel valued as a result of their positive relationships with staff. Leaders have created an inclusive and caring environment where pupils recognise their cultural diversity and welcome new arrivals into the school’s caring community. All pupils benefit from a rich curriculum which is carefully planned to reflect their needs and interests.”
“The school has a strong Christian ethos firmly centred on distinctly Christian values. This has created a school community in which every member is loved and cared for as a child of God. As a direct result, pupils at St Barnabas’ achieve and progress to the best of their individual abilities, both academically and socially.”
Please note: copies of all documents on this website are available from the school office.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Barnabas’ C of E Primary School
I am Beccy Harris and I am delighted to be the headteacher of St. Barnabas CE Primary School. We are a one-form entry school for children aged 3-11, set in the heart of the city of Oxford, and surrounded by its most famous landmarks and institutions.
We are a happy, inclusive school, rich in diversity and community spirit. Our pupils come from the local communities of Jericho and Summertown as well as from further across the city. We also welcome families from all over the world who are brought to Oxford to work and study. Our diverse international perspective gives the school the St. Barnabas vibrancy that we are so well known for.
Our school is a warm empathetic environment where children flourish in all aspects of their development. Children build good relationships, feel valued and are listened to. We cherish them as unique individuals with their own particular talents and enthusiasms. We strive to make school inspiring, enjoyable and a great place to create lifelong childhood memories.
We are a dynamic and newly formed staff team with a highly successful first year and a half under our belt. The local authority has commended us on our progress.
‘The newly formed leadership team has had a great impact on the education at St Barnabas that children receive. The leaders have continued to improve the school at pace’.
We have demonstrated our commitment to high academic outcomes. Statutory assessments for 2024 show significantly higher outcomes in all year groups. Our Year 6 SATs results are now well above national average with an impressive 90% achieving the standard in Maths and 42% achieving the higher standard in Reading and Maths. This has been achieved by focusing on a stimulating and engaging curriculum that is delivered through excellent teaching by inspiring teachers.
Please click here for more information about our Year 6 SATs results.
See local press coverage by clicking here.
In March 2025, we had our Ofsted Inspection and are delighted to announce that Ofsted has awarded us a ‘GOOD’ grading in all areas. Leadership is summarised as having ‘high ambitions and expectations’ that secure strong academic outcomes. The school is described as a ‘happy place to be’ with ‘warm relationships’, ‘kindness’ and ‘harmonious social times’. It is also noted that we offer ‘a range of opportunities to nurture talents and interests’ and have ‘a strong emphasis on pupil’s character, individuality and personal development’.
As we press on from ‘GOOD’ to great, we are developing creative strategies to challenge our learners further. We have enrolled in the Challenge Framework (NACE); and are working towards ‘The Challenge Award’ which recognises high quality provision for more able pupils. We are awaiting our assessment visit.
The school has undergone a makeover with a magnificent new community art piece completed by Lisa Made it. The grounds are being developed, and in the next two weeks we are installing a large sandpit, a mud kitchen, an outdoor workshop and a designated forest school shelter. A sports cage will be installed in 2025/26. Watch this space!
We are a fully inclusive Church of England school welcoming children of all faiths and world views. Children are encouraged to explore moral and spiritual values through their own lens’ and are given the space to consider the bigger questions in life. This helps them grow a deeper understanding of themselves and the world around them giving them a strong sense of themselves, their purpose and future direction. Our religious education and collective worship is respectful and fully inclusive with all children in mind.
After consulting with the school community we have a new school vision. The full version will be uploaded shortly but here is a summary.
‘They will soar on wings like eagles’’ (Isaiah 40:31)
Through values that create AWE-some individuals, we will become A (Adventurous) W (Wise) and E (Encouraging).
Look out for our new school logo which is coming soon!
Please look at our school video (below) . In the meantime, take the time to explore the website for information about the school. Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any questions or would like to find out more. We look forward to welcoming you to our school soon.

pageCache.text:
Meet Our Governors
Governors have a strategic planning role, responsibility for school governance, and supporting the Headteacher, who has responsibility for the day to day running of the school. We are required to follow legal and procedural processes laid down by the Government, in accordance with Church of England regulations.
We are always happy to hear from parents about issues which fall into this remit. If you would like to contact a member of the Governing Body please email Charlie Arbuthnott (Interim Chair of Governors) at chairofgovs@st-barnabas.oxon.sch.uk and she will be happy to help.
What do Governors do?
Governors are all volunteers and have a close working relationship with the Headteacher and staff to ensure statutory requirements are met, including:
Governors attend full Governing Body meetings four time a year, and to belong to Sub-committees of the Governing Body. The two Sub-committees are Finance, Staffing & Premises, and Curriculum, Standards & Pupils. Governors visit the school to get to know the staff and children and to see how the school operates. Minutes of Governors’ meetings are available in school. All school policies are available online.
Who are the Governors at St Barnabas?
Our Governing Body is made up of Parent, Local Authority, Foundation and Staff Governors. The number of each group of Governors is laid down in the School Constitution. Parent Governors are elected by the parents and must have a child in school at the time of election. Staff Governors work at school and are elected by the staff, both teaching and non-teaching. Local Authority Governors are appointed by the Local Authority. They may be County or City Councillors, or people known within the local community. Foundation Governors are appointed by the Church through the Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St Barnabas Church Oxford and the Diocese of Oxford, helping ensure the Christian vision and ethos of the school are upheld. The Governing Body of St Barnabas’ Primary School is comprised of:
The current Vicar of St Barnabas Church is Father Christopher Woods. He is supported by colleagues including Jenny Pittaway (Lay Minister).

Run Jericho started in 2011 and is organised by the St Barnabas Primary School Parent Teacher Association. It is a huge event that attracts people from Oxford and beyond. In 2025, the event raised a record-breaking £24,157.99 for the school and saw thousands of runners participate. This well-loved community event has certainly grown significantly from its humble beginnings and reflects the school’s message on inclusivity, healthy living and bringing the community together.
The next Run Jericho will be taking place on Sunday, 13th June 2027. Please check out the website and Facebook and Instagram pages for more information about the run, courses etc. and to register, volunteer or sponsor this lovely event.

pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
‘They will soar on Wings like Eagles’ Isaiah 40:19
Values: ‘To be AWEsome – Adventurous, Wise and Encouraging’.
We are a happy inclusive school, set in the historic Jericho area of central Oxford . With Oxford’s world renowned institutions on our doorstep and surrounded by hidden local treasures such as the canal and Port Meadow, we take advantage of our unique surroundings to provide opportunities that can’t be rivalled. With families visiting from across the globe to work and study in Oxford and over 30 languages, we bring a unique international perspective to all we do. Our children really are citizens of the world!
As well as delivering a knowledge rich curriculum with strong outcomes for all children, we cultivate a passion for learning, inspire curiosity and builds self confidence and an adventurous spirit. Our aim is for all our children to be the best they can be and to ‘soar on wings like eagles’. Our values of Adventure, Wisdom and Encouragement underpin all aspects of learning as we prepare the children for secondary school and the wider world.
All children access their full curriculum entitlement with appropriate support and challenge. Teaching is dynamic and responsive with continuous adaption to meet need. We draw on the work on The National Association for Able Children in Education (NACE). We are currently working towards our NACE Challenge Award to further develop the challenge and stretch we offer.
Our curriculum is ambitious and goes beyond the requirements of the National Curriculum. We have adopted the Cornerstones Curriculum 22 – a broad and balanced, knowledge-rich curriculum – which we deliver through exciting projects that build on prior learning and enable key knowledge and concepts to be rigorously reinforced. Under umbrella themes, such as ‘Frozen Kingdoms’ and ‘Emperors and Empires’, there are subject-specific projects that cover science, history, geography, art and design and technology. The remaining foundation subjects are taught discretely using carefully constructed curriculums created by experts.
Maths is delivered through the White Rose Maths scheme, with supporting materials taken from quality enrichment and extension programmes. Our new English curriculum is built around clear, progressive programmes of study with a carefully selected range of high quality texts supporting each unit of work. For phonics and early reading we follow the Little Wandle, Letters and Sounds programme.
Our curriculum is further strengthen by our teaching and learning framework which is underpinned by the foundations of best practice. Like other schools we draw on the work of Rosenshine’s Principles of Instruction, but also more specifically draw on the latest research from the Education Endowment Foundation, The Bell Foundation and The National Association for Able Children in Education. The above research is thoughtfully summarised in our teaching and learning framework often referred to as ‘The St. Barnabas Top Ten’ approaches.

pageCache.pageTitle: School History – St Barnabas C of E Primary School
pageCache.text:
St Barnabas’ Primary School, Oxford was founded as a Church School in 1854 by St Barnabas Parish and is now financed by the Oxfordshire County Council in partnership with the Diocese of Oxford, which is part of the Church of England.
The school moved to its present site in 1977. It was designed as a modern open-plan building, consisting of four teaching areas and a purpose-built nursery unit grouped around a central atrium-playground. Four new classrooms were added in 2002 together with new offices and a computer room to enable the school to become a full primary school in September 2003. There are two hard-surfaced playgrounds and a playing field. The hall and dining area were specifically designed for community use as well as school use.
St Barnabas’ School serves the community of Jericho and the area immediately to the north of the city centre. The school has a lively and involved PTA and good links with the parish church of St Barnabas and the community. We welcome children of all nationalities, ethnic groups, religions and world views. We regard the range of languages and the knowledge of other cultures within the school as a positive asset in our approach to a multi-cultural education.
Stained Glass Windows
The stained glass windows (illustrated at the top of this page) were created in 2006. The school were able to have the windows as an ex Chair of Governors Peter Corlett (See article below for more information on Peter Corlett.) left a generous donation.
The windows reflect the important link to St Barnabas’ Church and the diversity of the local Jericho community.
The Tudor Rose Emblem for St Barnabas
The emblem for St Barnabas’, among other things, is a shield shape with three rows of roses on it; the first row is of three silver Tudor roses on a red field, the second row two red roses on a silver field and the third is a single silver rose on a red field. In past times, clerks would celebrate St Barnabas’ day by making garlands of roses to wear and in Germany houses were decorated with ‘Barnaby’ garlands. This is likely to be linked to the time of year for St Barnabas’ day, 11th June.
When I was a pupil at St Barnabas’, we always went to church on St Barnabas’ day and we always wore red roses. My Gran would make sure that there was a rose or two in her garden and I would visit here before going to school to have my buttonhole pinned on me. After church we had the rest of the day off.
St Barnabas isn’t officially an apostle, he wasn’t one of the original 12, but his association with St Paul has meant that he has been given this status. As he travelled with Paul to spread the word and establish the early church, his statutes show him carrying a large book and a staff. When St Barnabas parish was created out of the parish of St Thomas (down by the station), St Paul’s was already in existence, so the new church was dedicated to St Barnabas’ in recognition of the partnership of Barnabas’ and Paul.
Historical Information
The new St Barnabas’ First School in 1977
The Bishop of Oxford came to open the school. The event was reported on in the local papers.
Mr Penrose was Headteacher when the school opened.
The Headteacher was Mr Penfold. from 30.04.73 – 31.08.85
John Purves (acting) Headteacher 01.09.1985 – 31.08.86
Keith Godfrey Headteacher 01.09.86 – 31.12.86
Hilary Hiorns Headteacher 01.01.87 – 31.08.02
Jane Thomas Headteacher 01.09.02 – 31.08.08
Fiona Hawkins Headteacher 01.09.08 – 31.08.19
Karen Donaghey Headteacher 01.09.19 – 31.08.22
Scott Lewis Interim Headteacher 01.09.22 – 31.08.2023
Beccy Harris Headteacher 01.09.2023
Building Work
The children at St Barnabas’ First School kept a record of the building work when the new school was built and opened in 1977. Two of the scrapbooks have been saved and are on display in the school.
Changes to the School
Throughout its time many changes have taken place with the school. New roofs across all of the old buildings in the Foundation Stage and KS1. The Nursery has been developed and now includes a disabled toilet. The school has been supported by the Diocese who have overseen all the building work.
The Playground
The field is very important in Jericho as after 4pm everyday it is shared with the community and during weekends and holidays. The field has had new equipment that is shared with the community a new climbing frame and trim trail, a table tennis table and a goal area. The PTA has worked tirelessly to raise funds for the trim trail and the climbing frame. The KS1 playground has a fabulous new climbing frame provided by the PTA.
Pictures below, from 1982, show the tortoise and snake that are still here today.
July 2019 – Sarah Fletcher has wonderfully repainted our snake and tortoise and the children are enjoying playing on them again. In 1981 St Barnabas’ School had a competition to design a playground sculpture. The winner was Sam Jones. The snake and tortoise were built by Class Two with their teacher Liz Burchfield. Sam who went on to become an artist/graphic designer sadly died in 2018 aged 44, but he will be remembered for creating something that has been played on by St Barnabas’ pupils over the past 40 years, and will be continued to be enjoyed in future. Thank you to Sam and the children from Class 2.
In 1977 there were no trees around the school field, but today that is a very different story (black and white photo), there is a photo in the early days of the school just after the trees were planted. The aerial photos were taken in 2002 and the trees have matured. Today we are grateful for the trees in summer as they provide a great deal of shade.
The Library
The pictures of the library below show it when the school opened in 1977 and how it is now. In 2021 the school was able to update the library with a significant donation towards the works made by a kind grandparent.
Peter Corlett 1931 – 2001
Although not born in Jericho, Peter became a Jericho person ‘by adoption’. When he retired from teaching for 35 years at St. Edward’s School he came to worship at St. Barnabas church and developed a great love of Jericho. After a few years he became Churchwarden and he was in that office when the appeal was launched to repair the tower. Peter devoted himself to this project and became ‘Clerk of Works’. The restored tower is something of a memorial to him. After retiring from the position of Churchwarden he was elected Chairman of the School Governors and threw himself wholeheartedly into the task giving great support to both staff and pupils. He could often be seen in Mrs Hiorns’ office on the phone to the Council in pursuit of a school improvement. Peter was infinitely kind and would help anyone in need, including supporting a family in Sheffield who wanted a better life for their children through education. In his spare time he played in the St Edwards’ school orchestra and wrote some of the earliest programmes for educational computer Maths games. Peter sadly died in January 2001, aged 69, after battling with cancer. One of his last acts was to send me flowers on the birth of my first child just a week earlier; kind and thoughtful to the end.
In his will Peter left a sum of money to St Barnabas’ school, some of which was used to purchase new staging for the hall, some spent over a number of years to fund building improvements, and some most obviously for the creation of the stained glass window in the foyer. This was devised and agreed by Peter’s sister, Pamela, and Fr Michael, Incumbent Vicar. It was dedicated and blessed in an unveiling ceremony in 2002, when the new wing of the school was opened as a Primary. The window reflects Peter’s belief that all people are equal in the sight of God, and his commitment to the multicultural nature and inclusive ethos of the school.
Peter’s ashes are in the memorial garden of St Barnabas church.
Chair of Governors 2001-2, 2011-16
